prompt_text:
1. Checkout my CwellEEGRead repo which is empty except a license file. 
2. Help me setup a reproducible research environment in this repo. Investigate the SysRevReproEEG repo which has a template to store all LLM prompts and session transcripts. Make it so that this prompt and all session transcripts are auto-archived from a Claude Code session into a top-level folder /llm-logs with one folder per claude session, and a sessions.csv file is listed in that directory. This first prompt should be listed in the prompts and its response should be there, too. 
3. Then help me install the doorstop traceability chain documents system in a python venv in this repo, but gitignored. We need the doorstop docs hierarchy in a top-level folder called docs then the doorstop document system lives in a subfolder called traceability.
4. Then write the first requirements: the program should convert Cadwell EEG formats from around the year 2020 and forward to EDF format. The development system will be given a few test EEGs in Cadwell format, and then the same test EEGs exported to EDF format by the native Cadwell application will be supplied for comparison, as well as the same test EEGs exported to a csv text format. The development system should have automated tests that prove equivalence between our EDF export and the native EDF export, as well as the equivalence between this systems EDF export and the text-exported EEG data.
5. Then investigate how we can use this BioSig toolbox to read Cadwell EEG, and also its licensing. We probably need to change the license if we are going to use the BioSig toolbox. The repo is here: https://git.ista.ac.at/alois.schloegl/biosig/-/tree/libbiosig-2.4.2/biosig4c++/t210
6. Then investigate the actual nature of Cadwell EEG files, as they are now in actual fact SQLite databases. I contributed to a discussion on a Matlabf forum previously, here: https://se.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/answers/480265-reading-clinical-eeg-ezdata-file-in-matlab . SQLite reading makes the outer structure of the data easier, but the inner format is not so clear, but the BioSig toolbox might help there. It would be preferable to port the code, even if it requires eating another licensing regime.
7. The eventual goal is to use have an easy way to have research EEGs which may have been recorded  for clinical purposes more easily analyzed by the SCORE-AI system (possibly in a command line tool that returns JSON) or by the Morgoth foundation model, here: https://bdsp.io/content/morgoth1/1.0.0/ , or to make a more modern plugin for EEGLAB / fieldtrip. The ultimate purpose has not been nailed down, but upstream of research use is conversion of proprietary Cadwell EEG format to the more standard EDF.  So there might be a uses/ folder. A possible uses/Morgoth folder might contain devops scripts to check out Morgoth and install+run it. A possible uses/EEGLAB folder might contain an EEGLAB reader plugin so a zip file can be generated (or as a later basis for a separate github repo for a Cadwell reader for EEGLAB).  A possible uses/SCOREAI folder might contain devops scripts to call a future SCOREAI program (supplied elsewhere) on our repo's EDF-converted Cadwell EEGs.


This is a long and complicated multi-part prompt, so you may prefer to use agents.
I think you are in the wrong repo. We only want to *read* the SysRevReproEEG repo, and the work itself should be in the CwellEEGRead repo. Verify.

OK, I now have supplied one cadwell test data file. It is committed under testdata/public/cadwell-export1, and is just noise data (no real patient data) but it has: a native EDF exported in subfolder /edf, a type of native export in subfolder native-export with a subfolder that the Cadwell system generated automatically called CadLink, and then a folder called "test" which contains the same EEG data exported as tab-delimited text. Do a git pull and investigate those files.
Do a git pull. The actual EDF files are now in the repo.
You now have another test dataset, which is real non-patient EEG. Proceed.

To answer your question about filtering, I now added another version of test export 3, with severe filtering (high pass 10 Hz, low pass 15 Hz) which I think should affect the EDF and the text export, but I am not sure. Do a git pull, then compare the two versions of "test 3"

Now let me double check something. Export-3 and Export3-with-filter were the exact same file. The only difference is: for Export-3 I opened Arc from the Arc database view on that EEG, right-clicked to ,"Export to EDF+" and "Export to text", and for for Export-3-with filter I opened Arc viewer from the Arc database view on the same EEG, set filters to 10-15, then right-clicked to "Export to EDF+" and "Export to text". Where there in fact any differences between export3 and export-3-with-filter?

Why do the text export time ranges differ? Did I do a SNAFU when exporting? Give me time ranges. Time ranges are supposed to be listed in the info.txt file (export 3 is right, export3-filtered is just a copy with a added note about filtering)

I expected all three versions of the export to cover the same time range, the whole range. But I see now in the dialog that the text export timeframe has a default that is less than the whole EEG. I exported the text file again, this time the whole range with and without filtering (zipped text). Re-do the analysis to compare filtered and unfiltered versions between EDF exports and text exports. Do we now have the same whole timerange, filtered and unfiltered, between the native file format, the native EDF export, and the text versions?
Pushed now, do a git pull and redo the analysis

Write me up a draft email to Jesper Tveit of Norwegian Holberg EEG AS , who is responsible for working on a solution for the SCORE AI EEG interpretation system to work with Cadwell EEG files, in which they intended to use Cadwell's native EDF export and then SCORE AI on those files. Mention the zero padding, the last frame drop, whatever you found about the initial filtering thing, the existence of this repo with its Python code, as well as the existence of the documented prompts system, the doorstop requirements and testing, and the MATLAB forum link, and my intention to publish this repo. Do it in English.

Apparently it is an issue that the Cadwell export is Cz-referenced (so, effectively bipolar). Most EEG systems have a separate "REF" channel, and I believe Cadwell does to, but it doesn't appear in the export. Investigate for the presence of a "REF" channel, and estimate if we can export the data as "REF" referenced instead of Cz referenced.
SCORE-AI consumes REF referenced data. From a regulatory perspective, this is a headache. If we make a synthetic reference, let's say common average, it is no longer the same data.
